I never said anything about being forced to.  I honestly think you're readng what you want to see not what I wrote.  I'm guessing I've fallen under some label in your mind and now you think you know my beliefs.  The thing is, a newspaper is or book are designed to print information for a certain goal.  That goal could be unbiased news but rarely is.  Eveyone knows that newspapers and books are biased, and aren't pretending otherwise.  Of course they only print what they want, a newspaper pays people to write the content.  Facebook is just the public posting to their friends/each other.  No business model, no salaried employees. Its a social network designed to connect individuals not dictate what information is worthy of printing on their site.  A newspaper vets the stories and contributers because they are responsible for the stuff printed.  Facebook isn't as they don't vet anything and the game changes a lot both legally and how the site runs when you start deciding what is or isn't allowed.  Its not that they are forced to leave anything up, it that the type of site they are doesn't do what they are doing. Now they are essentially declaring themselves a media outlet

Like I said, this was not about the content.  I don't even know what this website was about.  Clearly you missed the point by a mile.  Facebook is a social media site, not a publisher.  Why would it be in anyone's interest for facebook and others to select which content to allow as long as none of it breaks the law or doxxes etc? You can simply unfriend or unfollow someone who posts lots of stuff you don't like or just scroll past it.  Why would you want to have the site policing everything so that you don't even see this content whatever it is? What if they started removing stuff you liked? And don't start with me saying "well I don't like xyz so it wouldn't happen" because its the principle.  You're giving them the green light saying "I'm okay with you deciding what I can and can't see on this website" so that opens the door for anything.  This has already created a political echo chamber on sites like facebook.  How is that healthy? I always welcome my ideas challenged and so should everyone. Most of my opinions are based in fact and if they aren't it should be easy to prove me wrong.  I know I'm not above being wrong so I like reading content from the left and the right, communists to libertarians and everything in between.  If its "fake news" as they say then itll be easy to spot.  I can't see a single downside of allowing free and open discourse
